output.headline: Both of Privia Health's deals are in the target's own Health IT sub-sector and in its size band, and both closed.
output.differentiator: Its whole record sits in the target's sub-sector and size band, and every deal closed. Its median deal is larger than those of Evolent, Francisco Partners, TPG, Warburg Pincus and Veritas.
output.why_them: Same-sub-sector strategic with a fully closed record

acquirer_overview.title: A Health IT strategic with a short, fully closed record since 2017
points: Strategic buyer with 2 deals between 2017 and 2024; 2 of 2 (100%) closed [T:record, K:closed_share].
Median deal $231M, ranging from $205M to $256M; 2 of 2 deals sit in the comparable size band ($150M-$600M) [T:record, K:size_band].
Control deals were 1 of 2 (50%); only 1 deal has come since 2022, so the record is thin [K:control_share, K:recent].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Sub-sector focus and a technology-led buying motive point to this target
points: Share of its deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor in its likelihood; both deals are in Health IT [S:sector_share, K:by_sub_sector].
Technology Capability drove 2 of 2 deals, yet appears on only 10% of deals in the file, so it is a distinct motive [M:technology_capability].
Target margin close to what it usually buys is a modest factor for; having bought from this kind of seller is a slight factor against [S:margin_fit, S:own_fit_s].

precedent_activity.title: Two Health IT deals of $205M and $256M, both closed
points: Keystone Population Health: $205M minority investment, 2024, 20.2x EBITDA, 6.29x revenue [D:MA-2024-0128].
Select EHR Solutions: $256M SPAC merger, 2017, 20.9x EBITDA, 5.94x revenue [D:MA-2017-0427].
Neither deal was in the target's region; 0 deals in the National market, so the geography is untested [T:record, K:by_region].

valuation_context.title: Median multiple is the defensible anchor; Privia's history sits just below it
points: 13 comparable deals, all in the same sub-sector: 19.4x at the 25th percentile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the 75th [V:comps].
Target margin of 25.0% is above the comparable median of 22.2% but not in their top quarter, so the 50th percentile is defensible [V:comps].
Privia's median paid is 20.5x, below the comparable median. Synergy headroom is $14M-$23M; buyer revenue is not researched [V:comps, V:synergy].

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: The target's $300M EV exceeds Privia's biggest deal to date of $256M.
risk_flags.mitigant: Both prior deals sit in the $150M-$600M comparable size band, so the target is within range.
risk_flags.reality: Largest deal so far is $256M; this would be a new high for Privia [T:record, K:size_band, X:target].

risk_flags.title: Capacity unverified
risk_flags.concern: Buyer revenue is not researched and only 1 of 2 deals was a control deal.
risk_flags.mitigant: Synergy headroom of $14M-$23M supports a bid at the median multiple.
risk_flags.reality: Profile is not researched, so funding capacity stays unconfirmed until its financials are checked [V:synergy, K:control_share].

risk_flags.title: Outbid on price
risk_flags.concern: Its median paid of 20.5x sits under the comparable median of 21.4x.
risk_flags.mitigant: Its two deals were at 20.2x and 20.9x, close to the median anchor.
risk_flags.reality: Epic, Aledade and McKesson have paid more at the median, so Privia may be outbid [V:comps, D:MA-2024-0128, D:MA-2017-0427].

conviction.rationale: Two deals in the target's own sub-sector support the call, but no deal in the target's region and an unresearched profile keep it at Medium [C:conviction, T:record].
